messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — packaging bumped the private installer RC to rc-2026-03-20 due to slower-than-expected transport to customer mirrors. Holding public cutover until parity checks finish.

maria: Understood. Is this the mirror egress throttling we saw last week? any quick mitigation?

sanjay: Looks like it. The new offline bundle is ~18GB and the NFS edge nodes are hitting TCP backpressure in a few regions. We're exploring two short options: 1) split the bundle into chunked submanifests (smaller parallel streams) or 2) stagger the delivery window + increase retry/backoff.

devin: +1 on chunking. It keeps the delivery idempotent and lets the transporter resume specific chunks. Implementation sketch: update installer manifest to include "parts": ["m0","m1",...], add checksum per-part.

ops_jen: If we go chunking we need canary rules updated. Current deploy-bot can only approve whole-installer canaries. Can deploy-bot accept a partial manifest canary? cc @deploy-bot

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] received: canary-request for rc-2026-03-20. Current policy: whole-package canary only. To request partial canary, add label `canary:partial` to the manifest and post confirmation here.

maria: OK. I'll update the packaging ci to annotate the manifest with `canary:partial` when chunking is enabled. Also adding per-part sha256 to make parity checks fast. Example manifest snippet:```json
{"version":"epoch-v2","parts":[{"id":"m0","sha256":"..."},{"id":"m1","sha256":"..."}],"pin":"stable-private-2026-03"}
```

sanjay: Proposed rollout plan:
- 02:00 UTC: push chunked artifacts to staging mirrors (small subset)
- 02:20 UTC: run parity job (fast sha256 compare + cosign verify)
- 02:35 UTC: deploy-bot canary (partial) -> smoke test on 3 customer-like sites
- 03:10 UTC: if health ok, signal full propagation with staggered windows (per-region + 10m spacing)

devin: Rollback criteria: any checksum mismatch OR >2m average extra transfer latency on >33% of mirrors => abort and revert manifest alias to `stable-private-previous`. Revert command snippet (ops run):```bash
# pin back to previous manifest
redwood-release pin-manifest --alias stable-private-2026-03 --to stable-private-previous
```

ops_jen: Also ensure KMS signing keys are rotated on the signer service before full cutover. Cosign will fail open otherwise and cause avoidable aborts.

maria: Noted. I'll include a preflight that checks cosign status and `gcloud kms keys describe` (or equivalent) against signer. If cosign verification fails we won't flip the alias.

sanjay: Quick checklist for the window: chunked manifest + per-part sha256, deploy-bot partial canary label, cosign signer health, accelerate retry backoff for slow mirrors, and post-release note link.

devin: I put an initial release note draft here: https://docs.internal/releases/private-rc-2026-03-20 (please add transport metrics).

ops_jen: If we detect persistent backpressure after 2nd attempt we'll file a hotfix to repackage with gzip-level change and shorter chunk sizes. Aim to avoid immediate rollback unless parity fails.

maria: Added `canary:partial` tag to the staging manifest and kicked off the staging push. Monitoring job: `pkg-checker --manifest staging-rc-2026-03 --verify parts --cosign`

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] staging push registered. Canary ticket: #CANARY-874. Notifying oncall.

sanjay: Great. I'll watch parity results and post back in 15. If anything trips, we'll revert alias and call a rollback with the command above.

maria: parity: all parts matched for staging mirrors. avg transfer time reduced after chunking. proceeding to partial canary. :thumbsup:

devin: partial canary passed smoke tests on sites A/B/C. ready for staggered propagation at 03:10 UTC.

ops_jen: KMS and cosign checks green. I also bumped the transporter retry to exponential jitter to avoid synchronized retries.

sanjay: proceeding with staggered propagation now. Will post final once alias flips.

maria: alias flipped to `stable-private-2026-03` at 03:18 UTC. release note updated. Thanks team. :tada:

devin: quick post-mortem note: we should add a transport telemetry alert when single-mirror transfer latency exceeds baseline by 40% for >10m. That would have flagged earlier.

ops_jen: filed alert: ALERT-TRNS-502.

sanjay: Closing thread — tagging release:rc-2026-03-20 and linking to postmortem doc.
